A1.justification: Despite the changed title and organization, both PDFs describe the same research, benchmarks, metrics, and experiments. Their complete text, tables, figures, algorithms, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original autoformalization experiments, manual accuracy evaluations, metric validation, and ablations on ProofNet#, RLM25, ProofNetVerif, PDA, and MiniF2F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds Llemma-34B evaluations, including RLM25 results and expanded sampling analyses.

M1.justification: v3 Appendix A.6.1 reports that a fix for a generalized BEq+ false-positive exploit is now the implementation default. The fix is not specified in the PDF. Algorithm 1 and the sampling, type-check filtering, and selection procedures otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same benchmarks, training datasets, mathematical domains, and contextual test scenarios. RLM25 retains the same six projects and 619 pairs. The added Llemma-34B evaluations extend model configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Llemma-34B to the RLM25 model comparisons in Tables 4-6, including its greedy baseline. The selection-heuristic comparator set remains unchanged. GPT-4-turbo and Codex remain in Table 8 despite GPT-4-turbo disappearing from the main model-description subsection.

E3.justification: v3 extends the ProofNet# selection study up to 1,000 candidates to Llemma-34B and adds that model to existing RLM25 protocols. Shared prompting, temperature, splits, and final 50-candidate settings remain unchanged. Expanded annotation and hardware descriptions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 extends context ablations and sampling analyses to Llemma-34B. Appendix A.6 adds a generalized tautology exploit and a prime/congruence false-negative case. The Gaussian-integer false-positive example, statement-length analysis, filtering ablations, and contamination study already appeared in v2.

E5.justification: v3 Section 3.1 newly states that BEqL and BEq+ were evaluated on ProofNetVerif only once, without tuning their design on that benchmark. This discloses an evaluation count rather than additional runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals, seed variability, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Llemma-34B RLM25 results include 0.79% BEq+ without context, 30.33% with proofs removed, and 33.4% with sampling. It becomes the highest-scoring RLM25 model in Table 6, above the retained GPT-4o result of 31.6%. Figures 2 and 5 add curves. Existing table values are retained; Llemma-34B's ProofNet# entries added to Table 6 already appeared in v2's appendices.

T1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a formal counterexample pairing n + n = 2 * n with an unrelated generic tautology. It also outlines the equivalence obligations behind a missed prime/congruence match. These extend the mathematical failure analysis without adding general theorems or completed proofs.

C1.justification: v2 presents an introduced sampling method, overlooked type-check filtering, and state-of-the-art gains as central contributions. v3 redefines the contribution around evaluation metrics, benchmarks, and standards, treating sampling as an evaluated existing approach and explicitly recommending evaluation across inference-compute budgets. The underlying benchmark and metric contributions are retained.

C2.justification: v3 expands explanations of BEq+ failures and discusses stronger proof search, reference dependence, and untackled proof autoformalization. It removes v2's hypothesis that retained theorems serve as implicit few-shot examples and its local-sampling motivation. The length-dependent recall limitation itself was already documented in v2 Appendix A.5.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands documentation of the annotation process underlying its results and datasets: error criteria, anonymization, grouped review, a single annotator, and approximately 200 human-hours. It also documents RLM25 selection criteria, REPL backporting, H100 configurations, runtime and API costs, licenses, and direct implementation links. v2 offered a brief correction recipe and an RTX4090 timing example.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts from proposing an overlooked sampling approach to evaluating established approaches through new evaluation resources, materially narrowing the method-novelty claim. Bibliographic changes are smaller: Wang et al. (2020) and Wilshaw (2025) are added, and the earlier DeepSeek-Prover reference is removed. Anonymous (2024) becomes Liu et al. (2024), the same cited work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Metric validation moves from the experiments section into Section 3 alongside ProofNetVerif; sampling is reframed, related work is reordered, and the discussion and appendices are reorganized around evaluation and documentation.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different layout, including two-column appendix prose and code examples. v2's sampling diagram is removed; the selection plot gains a third panel, Tables 4-6 expand, and plots change colors and placement. The comprehensive results table is consolidated onto one page with revised labels.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the evaluation more auditable through detailed annotation and compute disclosures, adds useful Llemma-34B checks, and explains metric failures more clearly. Most empirical evidence remains unchanged. These gains are limited by the unspecified BEq+ fix and its unclear relationship to reported scores, plus the stale Appendix A.7 statement that Llemma-34B was not run on RLM25 despite the new tables and curves.
